question: Should OpenClaw keep the documented Codex `homeScope: "user"` failure/recovery model, or should the Codex plugin change its runtime behavior to skip prepared-auth injection in user-home mode?
rationale: The PR deliberately limits itself to recoverability, while its updated documentation identifies a potentially contradictory Codex runtime behavior; choosing the permanent behavior belongs to the Codex/plugin product owner rather than this CLI repair.

options.title: Land recovery command; track runtime behavior separately
options.body: Accept the CLI logout path as the bounded recovery mechanism and open or route a separate owner decision for the user-home injection behavior.

options.title: Require a runtime fix first
options.body: Hold this PR until the Codex plugin changes user-home behavior so a prepared OpenClaw profile does not prevent startup.

recommendation.title: Land recovery command; track runtime behavior separately
recommendation.body: Accept the CLI logout path as the bounded recovery mechanism and open or route a separate owner decision for the user-home injection behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied PR context shows steipete owns the proposed CLI and Codex-harness documentation boundary and explicitly called out the unresolved runtime direction.
